title: How Motivation Relates to Generative AI Use: A Large-Scale Survey of Mexican High School Students
extended_summary:
This paper examines how high school students’ motivational profiles relate to their use of generative AI tools for learning in math and writing. The central question is whether students with different levels of self-concept and perceived subject value use AI in different ways, rather than whether AI improves learning outcomes.

The study used an anonymous online survey with 7,739 public high school students in Chihuahua, Mexico, narrowing to 6,793 students who had prior experience with generative AI and passed attention checks. Students reported motivation indicators and their frequency of using AI for different math and writing tasks, such as formula retrieval, step-by-step help, brainstorming, grammar improvement, and feedback. The researchers used K-means clustering to identify motivational profiles separately for math and writing, then compared AI-use patterns across profiles.

The analysis identified three profiles in both domains: Aspirational, Confident, and Disengaged. In math, Aspirational students most often used AI for step-by-step guidance and interpreting problems, Confident students used it more selectively, and Disengaged students showed the strongest shortcut-seeking pattern, including the highest direct answer copying. In writing, Aspirational students mainly used AI for brainstorming and outlining, Confident students for language and grammar improvement and feedback, and Disengaged students reported the lowest overall use. The paper concludes that AI use is domain-specific and shaped by motivation, arguing against one-size-fits-all AI integration and for more targeted, motivation-informed educational support.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI chatbots or large language model-based tools used for producing, transforming, or supporting text and language tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Surveyed high school students’ self-reported use of generative AI tools in writing tasks (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, grammar improvement, feedback) and math tasks; the paper did not name a specific product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a large-scale survey study with self-reported usage patterns, not an experimental evaluation of instructional impact. It provides descriptive correlational evidence rather than causal evidence on reading or literacy outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No achievement effect sizes or literacy outcome improvements were reported. The paper’s contribution is about patterns of AI use by motivational profile, so instructional impact on literacy is unclear.
